comparator.sourceNotes: Reconstructed from the official Maastricht University SBE Outline Study Programme 'Bachelor Econometrics and Operations Research 2026-2027' (s0), which is based on the Bachelor Education and Examination Regulations and states the credit rules: each of the first four semesters comprises eight compulsory 6.5-EC courses and two compulsory 4-EC skills trainings (60 EC per year); semesters five and six comprise a 26-EC study-abroad period, one 4-EC disciplinary skills training, two 6.5-EC disciplinary courses, one 6.5-EC elective course and a 10.5-EC Bachelor's thesis written in semester six. Year 1 = Quantitative Introduction to Business, Analysis I, Linear Algebra, Microeconomics, Macroeconomics, Analysis II, Probability Theory, Finance and the skills Philosophy of Science and Responsible Econometrics; year 2 = Optimisation, Macroeconomics and Finance, Programming, Game Theory and Economics, Mathematical Statistics, Operations Research, Econometric Methods I, Economics of Uncertainty and Information and the skills Second-year Project I and II; each year totals 60 EC and the pathway 180 EC. The programme has no formal routes, tracks or specialisations, so no route is selected. The 2026-2027 outline does not name the year-3 disciplinary skills training, the two disciplinary courses or the elective; they are preserved as generic components with their stated EC rather than filled with named courses. The programme page (s2) and the curriculum page (s1, labelled 2024-2025) describe the identity (economics, computer science, management and statistics combined with maths; two core fields, econometrics and operations research) and, for an earlier year, list Introduction to Software in Econometrics or in Operations Research plus two of Auctions and Electronic Markets, Econometric Methods II, Advanced Algorithms and Actuarial Mathematics; these are used only as context for the evidence map and are not instantiated as components. Course-level content of the Maastricht course catalogue was not consulted, so comparator alignment relies on course titles, the programme descriptions and the stated credits. Three-year, English-language, full-time programme in Maastricht.

alternatives.concept: The strongest defensible UCR response to the Bachelor Econometrics and Operations Research at Maastricht University, which combines mathematics, probability and statistics, econometrics, optimisation and operations research, programming and economic theory and ends in a thesis. The programme rebuilds that quantitative core from UCR's mathematics track (calculus, linear algebra, probability and statistics, numerical methods, logic and discrete mathematics), statistics and UCR's one econometrics course, optimisation and decision-making courses in the AI and computer-science track (optimisation, planning under uncertainty, algorithms, advanced algorithms, reinforcement learning), data science and machine learning for prediction, and economics and finance courses for the economic context. It preserves genuine limitations: UCR has no operations-research or linear-programming course, no game-theory course beyond one part of Introduction to Economics, no economics-of-uncertainty course beyond parts of Microeconomics & Behavior and Behavioral Economics, no time-series econometrics and no actuarial mathematics.

alternatives.labelRationale: The completed curriculum has five courses in mathematics and discrete mathematics (Mathematical Methods, Linear Algebra, Advanced Calculus, Computational & Numerical Methods and Logic & Discrete Mathematics), three in probability, statistics and econometrics (Probability & Statistics, Research Methods & Statistics, Statistics & Experimental Methods) plus Econometrics, six in computing, optimisation and decision-making (Introduction to Programming, Optimization Methods in AI, Decision-making in AI, Algorithms & Data Structures, Advanced Algorithms and Reinforcement Learning), three in data science and machine learning (Introduction to Data Science, Machine Learning and Neural Networks & Deep Learning), and five in economics and finance (Introduction to Economics, International Macroeconomics, Microeconomics & Behavior, Behavioral Economics and Accounting & Corporate Finance), plus Personal & Professional Development. No single field dominates, so the label names the mathematical, statistical, optimisation and economic strands, and 'closest match' makes clear that UCR offers no econometrics-and-operations-research degree curriculum: it has one econometrics course, no operations-research course and no full game-theory or actuarial course.

alternatives.concept: A genuinely different route built on the programme's named application fields, finance and financial risk and marketing analytics, rather than on its operations-research and optimisation core. It keeps a lighter quantitative base (calculus, linear algebra, probability and statistics, regression, one econometrics course, data science and machine learning) and shifts the organising priority to using econometric and data methods on financial and market questions, supported by money, banking and finance, accounting and corporate finance, market research, marketing and consumer behaviour, public and behavioural economics and the economics of AI. UCR has no financial-econometrics or time-series course and no operations-research course, so the programme applies general statistical and econometric methods to finance and marketing rather than reproducing a financial-econometrics curriculum.

alternatives.labelRationale: The completed curriculum has eight courses in economics (Introduction to Economics, Microeconomics & Behavior, Public Economics, International Macroeconomics and Behavioral Economics, plus Econometrics, Money, Banking & Finance and Accounting & Corporate Finance), four in marketing, market research and business (Entrepreneurship & Business Foundations, Market Research, Marketing & Consumer Engagement and Business & Economy in the Age of AI), five in mathematics, statistics and research methods (Mathematical Methods, Probability & Statistics, Research Methods & Statistics, Statistics & Experimental Methods and Linear Algebra), and six in data, computing and decision-making (Introduction to Programming, Introduction to Data Science, Machine Learning, Neural Networks & Deep Learning, Database Management Systems, Decision-making in AI), plus Personal & Professional Development. The label names the applied economics, finance and marketing focus first and the data skills second; it does not claim a finance or econometrics degree.
alternatives.distinctnessRationale: Alternative 1 organises the programme around the target's mathematical and optimisation core: logic and discrete mathematics, numerical methods, advanced calculus, optimisation, planning under uncertainty, reinforcement learning, algorithms and advanced algorithms. Alternative 2 changes the organising priority to the target's named application fields, finance and marketing analytics (registry rows 5759 and 5760), and replaces those technical strands with finance, business and applied economics. The seven courses that differ from Alternative 1 (Entrepreneurship & Business Foundations, Money, Banking & Finance, Market Research, Marketing & Consumer Engagement, Business & Economy in the Age of AI, Public Economics and Database Management Systems) are consequences of that concept: the first is the formal prerequisite for Money, Banking & Finance and Market Research, and the others implement finance, marketing analytics, applied economics and market-data handling. They replace Logic & Discrete Mathematics, Optimization Methods in AI, Computational & Numerical Methods, Algorithms & Data Structures, Advanced Algorithms, Reinforcement Learning and Advanced Calculus in the closest match. The two programmes share 17 courses (mainly the mathematics, statistics, econometrics, data-science and core-economics base) and each has seven courses the other lacks, above the four-course floor.

progressionAssessment.rationale: Foundations precede the courses that build on them wherever the schedule allows: Introduction to Programming (semester 1) precedes Optimization Methods in AI (2), Algorithms & Data Structures (3), Advanced Algorithms (4), Decision-making in AI (5) and Reinforcement Learning (6); Mathematical Methods (2) precedes Linear Algebra and Probability & Statistics (3), Computational & Numerical Methods and Neural Networks & Deep Learning (4) and Advanced Calculus (6); Research Methods & Statistics (2) and Probability & Statistics (3) precede Statistics & Experimental Methods (5) and Econometrics (6); Introduction to Economics (1) precedes International Macroeconomics (3), Microeconomics & Behavior (4) and Behavioral Economics (6); Introduction to Data Science (2) precedes Machine Learning (5). Advanced Calculus can only run in semesters 2 or 6 and needs Mathematical Methods first, so it sits in semester 6. Formal prerequisites are all satisfied and every course sits in a semester in which it is offered. Personal & Professional Development is in year 1.

alternativeSelection.assessment: Alternative 1 owns ten generator-eligible rows that describe the programme's own core (5746, 5747, 5748, 5749, 5750, 5751, 5753, 5755, 5756 and 5766): using mathematics to understand economics and business, predicting economic and business trends, making organisations and systems more efficient, econometrics, operations research, mathematical reasoning and proof, probability and statistics, optimisation, programming and algorithms, and independent quantitative research. One further candidate direction was assessed. Applied econometrics for finance and marketing analytics (rows 5759 and 5760, supported by curricular rows 5754 and 5758) passed evidence, coherence, distinctness and feasibility and became Alternative 2: both rows are direct programme interests naming finance and marketing as recurring application fields, and UCR offers finance, market-research, marketing and economics courses; it shares 17 courses with Alternative 1 and differs in 7. No third alternative was defensible. Every generator-eligible row is either covered by the closest-match core or assigned to Alternative 2; the remaining rows are support-only curricular topics (5752, 5754, 5757, 5758, 5761 to 5765) or search-only outcome rows (5767 to 5771) and cannot generate a direction. A further concept built on optimisation, algorithms or machine learning would only re-sort the courses of Alternative 1 and would share at least 21 of its 24 courses, so it is not substantively distinct. Both included alternatives passed the 30-EC pairwise floor and mechanical feasibility against the enriched workbook.

comparisonAlignment.rationale: Mathematical Methods covers differentiation and integration, the single-variable calculus that Analysis I builds on; it does not reproduce Analysis I's rigorous real-analysis treatment.
Linear Algebra covers matrices, vector spaces and linear transformations, the same subject as the target's Linear Algebra.
Advanced Calculus extends calculus to several variables and differential equations, the identifiable multivariable content of Analysis II; it is applied rather than proof-based.
Probability & Statistics teaches probability theory and distributions, the primary subject of Probability Theory; it adds estimation that belongs to Mathematical Statistics.
Research Methods & Statistics covers inferential statistics, the estimation-and-testing part of Mathematical Statistics; it is an applied introduction without the target's mathematical derivations.
Econometrics teaches OLS, GLS and instrumental variables with tests and an empirical paper, the core content of Econometric Methods I.
Introduction to Programming teaches Python programming and problem solving, the subject of the target's Programming component.

Optimization Methods in AI covers search and optimisation methods; it addresses part of Optimisation's subject (numerical and combinatorial optimisation) but not its mathematical-programming and duality treatment.

Decision-making in AI covers planning and optimising behaviour under constraints and uncertainty, an identifiable part of Operations Research's decision-model subject; it is not a linear-programming, network or queueing course.
Introduction to Economics covers game theory and market structure in its microeconomics part, an identifiable part of Game Theory and Economics; UCR has no dedicated game-theory course.
Microeconomics & Behavior covers consumer choice, market structures and strategic behaviour, the subject of Microeconomics at a more advanced level.
International Macroeconomics covers national income, growth, inflation and policy, the same subject as Macroeconomics.
Accounting & Corporate Finance covers financial statements and corporate financial decisions, an identifiable part of Finance; it is accounting-led and lacks asset-pricing content.
Money, Banking & Finance covers financial markets, risk and financial decisions, an identifiable part of Macroeconomics and Finance; it does not offer its macro-financial modelling.

notes.text: Both programmes include substantial study of mathematics, probability and statistics, and economics. The Bachelor Econometrics and Operations Research additionally includes specialist work in operations research, mathematical optimisation, game theory, the economics of uncertainty and information, and a further econometric methods course. UCR students can instead combine mathematics, statistics, one econometrics course, optimisation and decision-making courses in the AI and computer-science track, and data science, but those specialist components are not offered at the same level of depth.

The Bachelor Econometrics and Operations Research is organised as a fixed sequence of compulsory quantitative courses in years 1 and 2, followed by a year-3 with a study-abroad semester, disciplinary courses, an elective and a thesis. At UCR, comparable subjects are distributed across courses in mathematics, statistics, economics, computer science and AI. The UCR programmes therefore cover related territory through a different curricular structure rather than reproducing the target course by course.
